title: Layers basics
summary: Add, rename, paint on and hide a layer.

steps.say: Press Control L to show the Layers tab at the lower right.

checks.prompt: Is the Layers tab visible, listing at least one layer?

hints: Windows, then Dockable Dialogs, then Layers opens it from the menu.
Press Tab if all the side docks are hidden.
steps.why: The Layers tab is where you see and control every part of the image.

steps.say: Press Control Shift N, then click OK in the New Layer dialog.

checks.prompt: Is there a new layer listed above the photo in the Layers tab?

hints: Layer, then New Layer in the menu bar opens the same dialog.
Set Fill with to Transparency so the new layer does not cover the photo.
steps.why: New marks go on their own layer so the photo below stays untouched.

steps.say: Double-click the new layer's name, type Sketch, and press Enter.

check.prompt: Is there a layer named Sketch in the Layers tab?

hints: Double-click the name text, not the small thumbnail.
Layer, then Edit Layer Attributes also lets you rename it.
steps.why: Clear names make layers quick to find later.

steps.say: Press P for the Paintbrush and paint a few strokes on the image.

check.prompt: Are there new brush strokes on the image that were not there before?

hints: Press D to reset the paint color to black.
Press the right bracket key for a bigger brush.
steps.why: Painting on the Sketch layer keeps your marks separate from the photo.

steps.say: Click the eye icon to the left of Sketch to hide that layer.

check.prompt: Are the brush strokes hidden now, with the eye next to Sketch turned off?

hints: The eye is in the first column of each row in the Layers tab.
Make sure you click on the Sketch row, not the photo row.
steps.why: Hiding a layer lets you compare without deleting anything.

steps.say: Click the same spot again to bring the strokes back.

check.prompt: Are the brush strokes visible on the image again?

hints: The empty box where the eye was is still clickable.
Control Z also brings back the last change.
steps.why: Layers can be switched on and off as often as you like.
